article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Sativa / 30% Indica
Genetics: Animal Mints #9 × Kush Mints #11
Breeder: Seed Junky Genetics
THC Content: 23–30%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , limonene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Floral soap, mint, rose, pine, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Most cannabis names require imagination before the connection between label and aroma becomes obvious. The Soap does not. Fresh flower can release a strangely convincing mixture of expensive hand soap, rose petals, lavender, mint, pine needles, citrus peel, and clean perfume before a deeper layer of sweet dough and diesel begins to show itself. Seed Junky Genetics created the cultivar from Animal Mints #9 and Kush Mints #11 in collaboration with the Cookies organization, and it became a flagship selection for the Minntz brand. Commercial documentation tied to Cookies and Minntz continues to identify that precise parental combination rather than the simplified Animal Mints × Kush Mints description often used elsewhere.

The unusual aroma helped distinguish this marijuana from the flood of dessert hybrids arriving during the same period, but scent alone does not explain its staying power. Dense trichome-covered flowers, substantial THC potential, an energetic opening effect, and a comparatively quick bloom made the clone attractive to cultivators and consumers alike. Instead of behaving like a heavy mint-family strain from the first inhalation, The Soap often begins bright and mentally active before a softer physical relaxation develops underneath.
Genetics and Lineage

The original genetic formula is Animal Mints #9 × Kush Mints #11. Seed Junky founder JBeezy developed the cross as part of the Cookies/Minntz collaboration, with contemporary industry sources consistently crediting Seed Junky Genetics and Cookies for the cultivar. Perpetual Brands, which distributes Cookies genetics, lists the genealogy specifically as Animal Mints 9 × Kush Mints 11 and identifies Cookies, Minntz, and Seed Junky Genetics as the breeding team behind it.

Both parents belong to the wider mint-and-Cookies family, yet their combination produced something far less conventional than another sweet Kush hybrid . Animal Mints contributes dense flower structure, resin production, potency, dough, earth, and a powerful hybrid foundation. Kush Mints #11 adds cool mint, citrus, Kush, and additional vigor. Because both parents already carry strong dessert and Kush influences, it would have been reasonable to expect the offspring to lean toward cream, cookies, and gas. The keeper instead expressed an intensely floral, almost detergent-like aromatic profile that gave the cultivar its identity.

The Soap also became breeding material in later projects rather than remaining an isolated clone. Its unusual perfume, resin coverage, and vigorous hybrid character made it attractive for crosses seeking something other than straightforward candy terpenes. That influence has helped preserve the cultivar’s relevance even as the commercial cannabis market moved through successive waves of Runtz , Zoap , RS11 , Permanent Marker , and other modern exotic families.
Effects and Experience

The onset is one of the characteristics separating this hybrid from many Kush Mints descendants. Mental stimulation can arrive quickly, producing a sharper sense of focus, elevated mood, and a desire to become engaged with whatever is happening nearby. Conversation, music, housework, creative projects, or other low-pressure activities may feel easier to settle into. CommCan, which identifies its genetics as Animal Mints 9 × Kush Mints 11 from Seed Junky, specifically characterizes the flower as having a head-oriented high suitable for daytime use.

Relaxation appears later and generally remains secondary at moderate doses. A gentle body ease can develop without immediately eliminating motivation, giving the experience a functional quality despite the cultivar’s potent ancestry. Higher doses change the balance. Mental stimulation may become racy or scattered, while the physical component can deepen enough to make the session substantially less productive.

Potency varies significantly between farms. PURPLEFARM currently places its Seed Junky-derived cultivation at approximately 23–26% THC with 2–4% total terpenes, while other documented versions have reached into the upper 20s or beyond. Consumers with limited THC tolerance should therefore approach strong flower carefully, since excessive amounts may cause dry mouth, dizziness, racing thoughts, anxiety, or impaired concentration.
Medical Benefits

The relatively alert beginning may appeal to medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that does not immediately feel sedating. Smaller servings can preserve mental engagement while introducing enough physical relaxation to reduce the feeling of being wound up. The balance changes rapidly with dose, however, and potent batches may become far less functional when consumed heavily.

There are no clinical studies demonstrating that The Soap itself treats depression, anxiety, chronic pain , PTSD, fatigue, or another medical disorder. Strain names are also imperfect predictors of chemical composition because THC and terpene concentrations vary from one crop to another. Anyone using marijuana medicinally should consider the laboratory profile of the specific product, dose, medications, individual sensitivity, and qualified healthcare guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aromatic profile is the defining feature. Floral perfume, rose, mint, pine, and clean soap-like notes dominate the first impression. Sweet cake, vanilla, citrus, and fuel emerge underneath, creating an unusual contrast between something almost cosmetic and something unmistakably cannabis-like. CommCan describes its version as soapy with a hint of sweet cake, while commercial Cookies documentation emphasizes a similarly clean, sweet aromatic character.

Terpene chemistry varies with cultivation. PURPLEFARM identifies beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool as the three major terpenes in its current batches, with total terpene content reaching 2–4%. Another cultivated version lists limonene, caryophyllene, and myrcene as major contributors. Caryophyllene adds pepper and dry spice, limonene introduces citrus brightness, linalool supports floral and lavender-like qualities, and myrcene can deepen the earthy background.

The flavor begins cleaner and sweeter than the aroma might imply. Mint, citrus, floral vanilla, and mild cake appear early, followed by pine, herbs, pepper, and a darker diesel finish. Proper curing is especially important because the delicate floral top notes can disappear when buds become excessively dry, leaving behind a more ordinary mint-and-gas profile.
Growing Information

Authentic The Soap has historically circulated primarily as a clone rather than a widely released seed line, making verified genetics more important than simply buying seeds bearing the name. Nursery documentation for the Seed Junky cut places flowering at approximately eight to nine weeks and describes medium-sized plants with moderate stretch, dense flowers, and heavy resin coverage. Flowers can range from bright green to extremely dark purple as maturity approaches, often beneath a thick layer of pale trichomes.

The plant benefits from early canopy management because its hybrid structure can produce enough stretch to create uneven tops if left untouched. Topping and lateral training before flowering help distribute the major branches across available light. Once bloom is established, adequate airflow becomes increasingly important around the dense colas, and branch support may be useful as flower weight increases.

No original Seed Junky grams-per-square-meter or outdoor-per-plant yield figure is reliably published, so precise production numbers would create false certainty. Contemporary growers generally regard the cut as a moderate-to-strong producer rather than a low-yield boutique plant. Outdoors, an eight-to-nine-week bloom commonly places harvest near mid-October in compatible Northern Hemisphere climates, although actual flower maturity and local conditions should determine timing.
FAQ
What are the genetics of The Soap?
The original cultivar is Animal Mints #9 × Kush Mints #11. It was created by Seed Junky Genetics in collaboration with Cookies and became closely associated with the Minntz brand.
Is The Soap indica or sativa?
It is generally considered a sativa-leaning hybrid. The effects commonly begin with mental energy, focus, and mood elevation before developing a softer relaxing body component.
Is The Soap the same strain as Zoap?

No. Despite both names referencing soap-like aromas, they are genetically different cannabis strains . The Soap comes from Animal Mints × Kush Mints, while Zoap belongs to an entirely separate genetic family.
How strong is The Soap strain?

Modern examples commonly fall somewhere in the mid-to-upper 20% THC range. PURPLEFARM currently lists approximately 23–26% THC for its Seed Junky-derived cultivation. Other batches can test higher depending on environment and harvest.
What does The Soap taste like?

Expect floral perfume, mint, rose, pine, citrus, vanilla, sweet cake, and a lingering diesel or earthy finish. The distinctive floral-clean quality is the main characteristic separating it from more conventional Kush Mints hybrids.
Final Thoughts on The Soap

The Soap earned its place in modern cannabis without depending on a familiar fruit or dessert profile. Seed Junky Genetics crossed Animal Mints #9 with Kush Mints #11, two parents already associated with dense resinous flower and high potency, yet the keeper expressed something unexpectedly floral. Rose, mint, pine, perfume, sweet cake, and diesel converged into an aroma strange enough to justify one of the more literal names in contemporary marijuana breeding.

Its performance gives that aromatic novelty substance. The hybrid combines an energetic cerebral beginning with later physical ease, can reach substantial THC levels, flowers in roughly eight to nine weeks, and develops dense trichome-heavy buds capable of dramatic purple coloration. For anyone exploring the Seed Junky and Cookies era of genetics, The Soap is an important cultivar because it demonstrates how closely related mint-family parents can produce something dramatically different from the creamy Kush profile their pedigree might predict.
